source_evidence: Investment-grade bonds are considered more likely than non-investment grade bonds to be paid on time.
question: Misconception: An investment-grade credit rating guarantees that a corporate bond will be paid on time.
answer: A credit rating is an evaluation of default risk, not a guarantee. Investment-grade bonds are considered more likely than non-investment-grade bonds to be paid on time, but a company can still default, and ratings may change as conditions or expectations change.
